statement: This record remains negative evidence on build 26200.8246: the repo did not produce enough supporting proof to promote it into a normal actionable surface.

anticheat_risk.anticheat_details: Long-DPC threshold tuning changes kernel latency/diagnostic behavior; anti-cheat and DRM compatibility should be reviewed explicitly.

gating_reason: Cross-layer evidence is strong, but an explicit policy or supportability gate still blocks promotion.

links.title: Repo system docs assign LongDpcQueueThreshold = 3 and LongDpcRuntimeThreshold = 100
links.summary: Repo docs list both values under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel` and map them to `KiLongDpcQueueThreshold` and `KiLongDpcRuntimeThreshold`.

links.title: Observed baseline existence for LongDpcQueueThreshold and LongDpcRuntimeThreshold
links.summary: The observed clean baseline confirmed that `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel` exists while both `LongDpcQueueThreshold` and `LongDpcRuntimeThreshold` are absent.

links.title: Current-build string hits for LongDpcQueueThreshold and LongDpcRuntimeThreshold
links.summary: The broad current-build string batch found exact Unicode hits for both value names in `C:\\Windows\\System32\\ntoskrnl.exe`, with no supporting hits in the adjacent `smss.exe`, `winload.exe`, or `ci.dll` probes.

links.title: Lightweight runtime batch kept both LongDpc thresholds in residual negative-result hold
links.summary: The tools-hardened lightweight runtime lane explicitly armed both values from missing to `1`, rebooted once, and still kept both `system.kernel.long-dpc-queue-threshold` and `system.kernel.long-dpc-runtime-threshold` in the residual `zero-exact-target-hits` hold.

links.title: Source-enrichment keeps both LongDpc thresholds as docs-first new candidates
links.summary: Source-enrichment assigns both values the same low-support docs-first route bucket and converges on the same suggested next runtime family: `timer-dpc-stress`, low priority, `windbg` queue.

links.title: Repo guest tooling now exposes a dedicated timer-dpc-stress harness
links.summary: The guest mega-trigger runtime script now exposes `timer_dpc_stress`, and the generic Procmon guest tool now exposes `TriggerProfile = timer-dpc-stress`; both align directly with the enrichment recommendation for `timer-dpc-stress` triggers by combining timer-resolution changes, concurrent timers, and DPC-heavy workload.
